questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Container Queries”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Media queries versus container queries” under “Container Queries”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with container queries?
options: Define a query container and test the component in both narrow and wide parent contexts.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Define a query container and test the component in both narrow and wide parent contexts.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Define a query container and test the component in both narrow and wide parent contexts. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Container Queries” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
